bottom_line: In TRILOGY ACS, prasugrel versus clopidogrel did not significantly reduce the primary end point in patients under 75 years (hazard ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.05).
implications: In patients with unstable angina or NSTEMI managed without revascularization, these data do not show a statistically significant reduction in the primary composite end point with prasugrel versus clopidogrel (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.05; P=0.21). The confidence interval includes 1.00, so a benefit or no difference is compatible with the primary result; a prespecified recurrent-events analysis suggested lower risk (HR 0.85; P=0.04), while severe and intracranial bleeding rates were reported as similar between groups.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial comparing prasugrel vs clopidogrel in medically managed NSTE-ACS (no revascularization).
Primary analysis population: 7243 patients under 75 years receiving aspirin; evaluated up to 30 months.
major_points.quote: in a primary analysis involving 7243 patients under the age of 75 years receiving aspirin, we evaluated up to 30 months of treatment

major_points.text: Prasugrel dosing and comparator dosing in the primary analysis.
major_points.quote: prasugrel (10 mg daily) versus clopidogrel (75 mg daily)

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point definition (in patients under 75 years).
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke among patients under the age of 75 years.

major_points.text: Primary end point result at median follow-up 17 months: no significant difference.
major_points.quote: At a median follow-up of 17 months, the primary end point of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke among patients under the age of 75 years occurred in 13.9% of the prasugrel group and 16.0% of the clopidogrel group (hazard ratio in the prasugrel group, 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 1.05; P = 0.21).

major_points.text: Prespecified analysis of multiple recurrent ischemic events suggested lower risk with prasugrel in patients under 75 years.
major_points.quote: The prespecified analysis of multiple recurrent ischemic events (all components of the primary end point) suggested a lower risk for prasugrel among patients under the age of 75 years (hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.72 to 1.00; P = 0.04).

absolute_effects.text: Primary end point at median follow-up 17 months in patients under 75 years: 13.9% vs 16.0% (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.79 to 1.05; P=0.21).
absolute_effects.quote: At a median follow-up of 17 months, the primary end point ... occurred in 13.9% of the prasugrel group and 16.0% of the clopidogrel group (hazard ratio ... 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 1.05; P = 0.21).

absolute_effects.text: Safety at 30 months (Age <75 years): TIMI Major 2.1 vs 1.5 (39 [1.1] vs 30 [0.8]).
New, nonbenign neoplasms in overall treated population: 1.9% vs 1.8% (P=0.79).
absolute_effects.quote: The frequency of new, nonbenign neoplasms in the overall treated population did not differ sig- nificantly between the pra­su­grel group and the clo­pid­o­grel group (1.9% vs. 1.8%, P = 0.79)

subgroups.text: Prespecified subgroups were used to explore consistency of treatment effect on the primary efficacy end point.
subgroups.quote: We explored the consistency of treatment effect on the primary efficacy end point in prespecified subgroups.

subgroups.text: Interaction with prasugrel treatment apparent in current/recent smokers, angiography before randomization, and proton-pump inhibitor at randomization.
subgroups.quote: an interaction with pra­su­grel treatment was apparent in cur- rent or recent smokers, those who underwent an- giography before randomization, and those tak- ing a proton-pump inhibitor at randomization

subgroups.text: In current or recent smokers (<75 years), event rates at 30 months were 11.7 vs 20.8 with HR 0.54 (0.39–0.74) and P value for interaction <0.001.

harms.text: Rates of severe and intracranial bleeding were similar between groups in all age groups.
harms.quote: Rates of severe and intra- cranial bleeding were similar in the two groups in all age groups.

harms.text: In patients <75 years, prasugrel had higher TIMI major or minor bleeding at 30 months (HR 1.54; P=0.02).
No significant between-group difference in frequency of nonhemorrhagic serious adverse events, except higher heart failure in clopidogrel group.
harms.quote: There was no sig- nificant between-group difference in the frequency of nonhemorrhagic serious ad- verse events, except for a higher frequency of heart failure in the clopidogrel group.
